title: Order States That Bear a Charge, and the Point of Payment
content:
A charge is raised against a Lift Tickets order only while the order stands in the ordered, paid or issued state. The state is taken from the collective's own record of that order, read before the charge is raised and matched to the order the charge is being raised against, rather than from the guest's account of where the order has got to.

| The order stands as | A charge may be raised against it |
| --- | --- |
| ordered | yes |
| paid | yes |
| issued | yes |
| in use | no |
| used up | no |
| expired | no |
| cancelled | no |
| refunded | no |
| closed | no |

The right-hand column follows from the rule alone: the three states named are the only ones in which a charge stands, so an order in any other state bears none.

## What the charge moves

The amount still to be collected for the order rises when the order or a fee is raised against it, and falls when a payment clears. An order stands paid once the money for it has cleared.

## When the money is taken

The product's payment point decides when the money is taken: at the order, or when the media is collected. Those are the two points the line is written for, and each product carries one of them.
